The receptionists are often abrupt, do not let you explain your situation, and frequently give incorrect information because they have not listened to what you are actually asking for.

Most recently, I called to ask about support for flight anxiety. I fully accepted that the practice could not prescribe a sedative and said so, but when 111 and a local pharmacy advised me to ring back to ask about alternative options, the receptionist repeatedly cut me off and simply restated that they “cannot prescribe a sedative”. Even after clearly explaining that I was not asking for a sedative but for an alternative, I was asked again if I wanted a sedative instead of being helped to explore other options.

I was then told I had to use an online link to contact the doctor and that I could not book an in‑person appointment for this, which left me feeling that basic access to care is being blocked by reception rather than supported.

Overall, I have found the reception team rude, unhelpful and unprofessional, and it feels unnecessarily difficult to get straightforward, compassionate care from this surgery.

On a positive note, Dr Burns, NP Caroline and mental health nurse Karen have all been kind, understanding and professional, and this makes it even more disappointing that the “front door” to the practice is so unwelcoming.

The surgery urgently needs to review how reception staff communicate with patients and how easy it is to access appointments and appropriate
